title: Neznaika's Adventures
author: Nikolai Nosov
short_summary: In a tiny town where everyone is the size of a cucumber, a cheerful, boastful boy named Neznaika (which means "Know-Nothing") is always getting himself and his friends into trouble by pretending to know things he doesn't. When his mistakes cause real problems for the town, Neznaika has to learn the difference between confidence and actual knowledge.
extended_summary:
In a tiny town where everyone is the size of a cucumber, a cheerful, boastful boy named Neznaika (which means "Know-Nothing") is always getting himself and his friends into trouble by pretending to know things he doesn't. When his mistakes cause real problems for the town, Neznaika has to learn the difference between confidence and actual knowledge.

Neznaika's adventures take him from a wild ride in a homemade hot-air balloon to a much bigger journey to the Moon, where he sees a strange society built entirely around money and greed. Along the way, his friends — patient inventors, doctors, and musicians — keep helping him out of trouble, even as he slowly realizes that being clever takes more than just talking big.

questions.explanation: Neznaika's name comes from his habit of claiming to know things he doesn't.

questions.prompt: Neznaika and his friends are all the size of a ___.
questions.explanation: The whole town is inhabited by tiny people no bigger than a cucumber.

questions.prompt: Sort each character into the right group.
questions.explanation: Znaika, the doctor, and the musician approach things carefully, while Neznaika often acts before thinking.

questions.prompt: Do you think Neznaika's confidence is a good thing or a bad thing? Explain.
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — the story shows both the fun and the danger of overconfidence.

questions.prompt: Neznaika's biggest habit — the one that gets him into the most trouble — is...?

options: Claiming he knows things he actually doesn't
Being too quiet and shy to ask for help
Never wanting to try anything new

questions.explanation: Neznaika's confidence is never in short supply — actual knowledge is the part he keeps running out of.

questions.prompt: Neznaika's biggest adventure takes him all the way to the ___, where he sees a strange society built on money and greed.
questions.explanation: It's a much bigger trip than his earlier homemade hot-air balloon ride — and a much bigger lesson, too.

questions.prompt: Put Neznaika's adventures in order, from smallest to biggest.

items: Neznaika boasts about things he doesn't actually know
His mistakes cause real trouble for the tiny cucumber-sized town
He takes a wild ride in a homemade hot-air balloon
He travels all the way to the Moon and sees a society built on greed

questions.explanation: Each adventure is bigger than the last — but the boasting-before-knowing habit that started it all never really changes.

questions.prompt: Match each character to their approach to problems.

right: Practices skill instead of boasting about it

questions.explanation: Neznaika's friends all share one trait he's still learning: doing the careful work before claiming the credit.

questions.prompt: Sort each of Neznaika's habits into the right group.

content.groupA: Something Neznaika is actually good at
content.groupB: Something Neznaika only pretends to be good at

options.label: Actually knowing how things work before trying them
Getting friends to like and forgive him
Being careful enough to avoid causing trouble

questions.explanation: Neznaika's real talents — charm and cheer — are genuine. It's the knowing-what-he's-doing part he still has to earn.

questions.prompt: Neznaika talks big before he actually knows what he's doing. Can you think of a time being extra confident helped you — or a time it got you into trouble, like it does for Neznaika?
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — confidence can push you to try new things, but it can also get ahead of what you actually know, just like it does for Neznaika.
